subject: ventures/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner
professional: an experienced ball python breeder who plans pairings for sale (with working reptile-genetics knowledge); they check first that single- and multi-gene Punnett odds match textbook ratios (1:2:1, 9-class dihybrid), then how possible hets ('66% het', '50% het') are handled, then the spider homozygous case, then whether the common allelic complexes (BEL: Lesser/Butter/Mojave; Cinnamon/Black Pastel; Yellow Belly/Gravel/Asphalt) are handled, then whether the money side (fees, raising cost, hatch rate) is arithmetic they would trust

evidence.correctness: Wrote an independent checker (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/c7bd76da-fba0-5582-91c4-a58d419f796f/scratchpad/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner/check.mjs) that models explicit diploid parent genotypes, treats a possible het as a mixture over the parent's genotype (fixed for the whole clutch), and enumerates gametes per genotype pair; ran `node /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-oss-monorepo/c7bd76da-fba0-5582-91c4-a58d419f796f/scratchpad/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner/check.mjs /home/user/oss-monorepo/ventures/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner/calc.mjs`. Per-egg odds match exactly on all five crosses: Pastel het Albino x Pastel het Albino gives the textbook 9 classes (1/4, 4x 1/8, 4x 1/16), Spider x Spider 50/25/25 dead, Super Pastel x Pastel 50/50, Spider het Pied x Clown 66.67% het Pied (Pied 1/6 per egg), and a 24-class trihybrid with a 50% het parent. Economics: Albino x het Albino hand check (8 eggs, 10% fee, $20 raise, $50 overhead -> profit 780) is reproduced in the suite and I agree with it by hand. But the clutch-level 'chance of at least one' (targetChance and each row's atLeastOne) multiplies per-egg odds as if eggs were independent, which is false when a parent is a possible het: its genotype is the same for every egg. Spider het Pied x Clown 66.67% het Pied, 6 eggs, 85% hatch, target Piebald: correct 0.5077, tool 0.6001. Luna (50% het Clown) x Ember (het Clown), target Clown: correct 0.3807, tool 0.4903, 11 points high. Rank-by-target uses this number, so it systematically favours pairings with unproven parents. Expected-value outputs (hatchlings, revenue, profit) are unaffected (linearity). Hence 2.
evidence.completeness: README/page features exercised in node: gene table with aliases and allelic groups (Hypo->Ghost, Pied->Piebald), animal parsing (visual, het, N% het, Super, Normal), price table with greedy morph-name match ('Super Pastel Yellow Belly'), every female x male pairing, expected hatchlings, revenue after fees, raising cost and overhead, rank by profit and by target chance, allelic refusal (Mojave x Lesser refused with a named message; Mojave x Mojave allowed and gives Super Mojave 25%), verifyPlan, CSV export, guide whose worked table is recomputed by page.test.mjs. All work; no TODOs. Served page https://marisstella.app/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner/ returns 200 (`curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}'`). Not modelled items stated (index.html:113).
evidence.verification: `cd ventures/ball-python-morph-pairing-planner && node --test '*.test.mjs'`: 40 tests, 40 pass, 0 fail (~330 ms). Five seeded mutations with platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 4 caught (possible-het gamete share 0.5*share -> share; selling fee dropped; hatch rate dropped from targetChance; raising cost on eggs instead of hatchlings, caught via verifyPlan), 1 survived (hatch rate dropped from each row's atLeastOne, calc.mjs:362). The 'independent gamete-pair oracle' (calc.test.mjs:84) reuses the same per-gamete t abstraction as the code, so it cannot catch the possible-het clutch-correlation error; verifyPlan re-derives targetChance with the same independence formula (calc.mjs:406-408). Not 3: the core clutch-level claim is checked only against a copy of its own assumption.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (441 lines), calc.test.mjs, page.test.mjs, index.html script (lines ~145-240). Pure functions, no dependencies, output through esc(); clear error messages for every bad input tried ('Super Spider' refused, '0% het' and '120% het' refused, duplicates named, 'poss het Clown' asks for a percentage). Minor: 'Pastel het Albino' without a comma is reported as an unknown gene called 'Pastel het Albino' rather than a hint to use commas; 'pos het Clown' (common spelling) not recognised; '66% het' gives t=0.33 rather than 1/3, so typed 66% is slightly off the 2/3 it stands for.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer and no-warranty text present (index.html:136), usage counter local-only with opt-out (index.html:140, usage.mjs), not-modelled list stated (index.html:113), served page loads. But the FAQ 'What does 66% het mean?' (index.html:123 and the FAQPage JSON-LD at index.html:12) says a possible het is 'a baby from a het-by-visual or het-by-het pairing' and 'Breeders also write 50% poss het for the baby of a visual and a normal'. Both are wrong genetics: the normal-looking babies of visual x het are 100% het (only het x het makes 66% hets), and visual x normal babies are 100% het; 50% possible hets come from het x normal. A user following that FAQ would enter a proven het as 50% and understate its odds. 'Checked against an independent gamete-by-gamete count' (README:24, index.html:113) is true for per-egg odds but the oracle shares the code's possible-het model.
evidence.fitness: Walked a breeder's job: three females, three males, rank pairings for a season by profit and by chance of a Piebald. The per-egg odds table and the profit ranking are usable and the CSV is handy. Gaps a breeder hits in the first hour: the BEL complex (Lesser/Butter/Mojave/Mystic/Russo), Cinnamon/Black Pastel and Yellow Belly/Gravel/Asphalt are among the most-bred genes and any pairing mixing them is refused; het and possible-het offspring cannot be priced (prices key on visuals only); offspring of a possible-het parent are shown as split 'het' and 'non-het' classes rather than as the possible-het percentage the breeder would advertise; and the target-chance ranking overstates pairings with unproven parents.
evidence.domain: Compared against standard Mendelian genetics (Punnett squares, any genetics textbook) and common ball python breeder convention (as used by the World of Ball Pythons and MorphMarket genetic calculators, from knowledge; not fetched). Right: recessive, incomplete-dominant, dominant and Super forms; spider treated as having no viable super (common convention, stated as 'reported'); Pinstripe dominant; allelic groups refused rather than guessed. Departures: clutch-level probability with possible-het parents treated as independent per egg; FAQ misstates where 50% and 66% possible hets come from; allelic complexes not modelled (the reference calculators handle them, e.g. Lesser x Mojave -> 25% BEL); spider wobble not mentioned anywhere although it is the first welfare question breeders raise about spider pairings (welfare is listed as not modelled).

defects.what: Clutch 'chance of at least one' (targetChance, used for rank-by-target, and each row's atLeastOne) treats eggs as independent even when a parent is a possible het, whose genotype is fixed for the clutch; overstates by 9 to 11 points on the sample pairings (0.6001 vs 0.5077; 0.4903 vs 0.3807) and ranks unproven-parent pairings too high

FAQ misstates possible-het origins: says 66% hets come from het-by-visual pairings and 50% poss hets from visual x normal; visual x normal and visual x het normals are 100% het, 50% possible hets come from het x normal
Test oracle and verifyPlan reuse the code's per-gamete t abstraction, so the clutch-correlation error cannot be caught; the atLeastOne row has no test (hatch-rate mutation survived)
Allelic complexes (BEL Lesser/Butter/Mojave, Cinnamon/Black Pastel, Yellow Belly/Gravel/Asphalt) are refused, though they are among the most-bred genes and reference calculators model them
Possible-het offspring cannot be priced or shown as the possible-het percentage breeders advertise; prices key on visual genes only
'66% het' (the breeder's shorthand for 2/3) becomes t=0.33 instead of 1/3, and the comma-free 'Pastel het Albino' and the spelling 'pos het' are rejected as unknown genes

verdict: Per-egg Mendelian odds are right on every cross recomputed independently (dihybrid 9-class, spider lethal, super forms, possible-het per-egg, a 24-class trihybrid), and the money arithmetic is right. It misses the bar on correctness, verification and claims: the clutch-level 'chance of at least one' ignores that a possible-het parent's genotype is shared by every egg, overstating the sample pairings by about 10 points and skewing rank-by-target, and the tests cannot see it because their oracle shares the same model; the FAQ also states the wrong origins for 50% and 66% possible hets. Refusing allelic complexes keeps it honest but leaves out a large share of real pairings.
